thread.title: Three Morehead State Eagles receive All-OVC honors in beach volleyball awards
thread.title_full: Three Morehead State Eagles receive All-OVC honors in beach volleyball awards

author: r. l. foster
title: Three Morehead State Eagles receive All-OVC honors in beach volleyball awards
text:
Three athletes from the Morehead State Eagles women’s beach volleyball team received All-Ohio Valley Conference honors, with Haylee DePonte becoming the first Eagle to be named league Freshman of the Year, according to an April 22 announcement.
The recognition highlights a strong season for Morehead State’s program and acknowledges individual achievements among its players. These awards reflect both athletic performance and contributions to team spirit.
DePonte, a redshirt freshman from Aiea, Hawaii, secured six victories at positions three and four this year. She partnered with Amelia Nott for three conference wins at No. 3 and was also selected for the All-Freshman Team. Head Coach Sarah Martin said, “Haylee has been a special addition to our program. She deserves this recognition, not just for her performance and work this spring, but also for the hard work she put in this fall to work to be the best player and teammate she can be. She’s a great teammate that shows up to support her partner and her teammates, and we are so proud she is Freshman of the Year.”
Junior Bella Marita earned second-team honors after holding down one of MSU’s No. 1 pair spots with ten victories this spring—including four in league play—making it her third consecutive season as an All-OVC selection at Morehead State. Martin said about Marita: “Bella has been a standout in our program since her freshman year. Her quickness in the sand and knowledge of the game has not only helped her to be a great player, but also to be a teammate that helps everyone around her be the best they can be. Bella is someone that makes her love of the game infectious, and is truly one of the best defenders I will have ever coached.”
Freshman Riley McCloskey from Newport, Kentucky played primarily at positions four or five during her first collegiate season and recorded five wins while earning All-Freshman Team status as well. Martin said about McCloskey: “Coming in, in her first semester at Morehead State and her first time playing in the sand, Riley truly put forth work to learn the game and improve. Her flexibility to play with multiple partners and be ready to be a blocker or defender has helped to make our team better in the sand every day, and she deserves the recognition for the impact she has made on our team this spring.”
Other major OVC awards included Chattanooga’s McKenna Faychak being named Player of the Year as well as Pair of The Year alongside Maddie Lecik; Chattanooga was also recognized as Coaching Staff of The Year.
